investigation.method: manual browser-driven review in Firefox from the homepage as a logged-out patient, with direct follow-up on surfaced routes and form entry pages
investigation.manual_browser_mode: headful Firefox using a disposable copy of the local profile

headline: New Bank still looks like a transition case, but the patient-task picture is now clearer. The homepage says all requests go through PATCHS from 1 October 2025, the appointments page still tells NHS App users to continue to the Accurx system, local Silicon Practice forms still render on the practice domain, and repeat-prescription and other admin routes remain available as separate local forms.

items.label: Public website stack
items.platform: WordPress with NHS UK theme and Silicon Practice elements
evidence: The public site runs on the standalone newbank.nhs.uk domain.
Live local form routes still exist under /form/ and /online-forms/.

items.label: Current promoted request platform
evidence: The homepage and appointments page say that from 1 October 2025 all requests made by phone, in person or online will go through Patchs Health.

items.label: Older app-mediated wording still on the site
evidence: The appointments page still tells NHS App users to select continue to the Accurx system.
That conflicts with the same page's PATCHS-first wording.

items.label: Legacy local forms still available
items.platform: Silicon Practice style local forms on the practice domain
evidence: The old medical-help form at /form/get-help-for-any-health-problem/ still renders live.
The prescriptions page still points to local repeat-prescription, prescription-question and pharmacy-nomination forms.

discovered_paths.label: Direct PATCHS route from appointments page

observed_workflow: The appointments page says all requests go through PATCHS.
It also says phone requests remain possible and that home visits should be phoned in before 10am.
Urgent medical issues outside normal hours are not clearly handled on the appointments page during this pass.
friction: The page gives mixed supplier instructions by promoting PATCHS while still telling NHS App users to continue to Accurx.
A patient has to interpret whether urgent same-day help should go to PATCHS, phone, or NHS App.

observed_workflow: Homepage to Appointments is one click.
Appointments to the direct PATCHS route is another click.
The site says patients should have received a text message with a registration link for PATCHS.
gating_or_preconditions: Probable registration or login barrier on the PATCHS route.
The site frames PATCHS account setup as something patients may need before go-live.
friction: Supplier overlap on the same page increases cognitive load.
The user has to choose between NHS App wording, PATCHS wording and phone wording.

initial_inputs_observed: Who are you completing this form for?
Please tell us about the problem
friction: This is a relatively high first-step data burden before the patient can explain the problem in context.
The coexistence of this local form with PATCHS muddies which route is current.

observed_workflow: The prescriptions page says the easiest route is the NHS account or NHS App.
It also exposes local forms for repeat-prescription requests, prescription questions and pharmacy nomination.
The page says prescriptions are ready after 2 working days unless a doctor needs to see the patient.
friction: Prescriptions are not fully consolidated into the PATCHS story.
The page still depends on several separate local forms for different prescription-related tasks.

observed_workflow: The homepage exposes Feedback and complaints directly.
The page title is Feedback and complaints and it shows a Complaints procedure heading.
friction: The page still sits under the wider transition banner and does not look especially prominent compared with the request-system messaging.

encountered_issues.details: Appointments page says all requests go through PATCHS but still tells NHS App users to continue to the Accurx system.
The old local medical-help form remains live on the practice domain despite the site's PATCHS-first transition messaging.
Prescription-related tasks are split across several separate local forms rather than a single consistent front door.

probably_true: New Bank is still in a mixed-transition state rather than having a clean single access pattern.
The main patient burden is not just multiple suppliers; it is multiple overlapping routes with different implied currentness.
needs_follow_up: Check the direct PATCHS route out of hours to see whether it stays available, queues the request, or visibly closes.
Check whether the complaints page content itself is stale beyond its title and heading.
Test whether the local legacy forms still submit or only render.
